thread.title: Tesla, Nvidia and FANG Lead Rout of Tech Stocks on Tuesday

author: thestreet.com
title: Tesla, Nvidia and FANG Lead Rout of Tech Stocks on Tuesday
text:
Tech stocks led the market down Tuesday, with autonomous vehicle makers and technology providers showing particular signs of weakness.
Nvidia Corporation's ( NVDA ) stock fell after the company confirmed that it is temporarily halting its self-driving car tests on public roads following a fatal crash involving Uber's autonomous vehicle in Arizona last week. Shares fell 7.8%, closing at $225.52.
Update: Nvidia tells CNBC that it is "temporarily suspending the testing of [its] self-driving cars on public roads to learn from the Uber incident" https://t.co/6EUbCjII3f pic.twitter.com/QJdAN3ylBz
— CNBC Now (@CNBCnow) March 27, 2018 Tesla, Inc. ( TSLA ) , which is also developing autonomous vehicles, dropped more than 8% Tuesday after the National Transportation Safety Board announced an investigation into a fatal crash involving one of the company's vehicles. 2 NTSB investigators conducting Field Investigation for fatal March 23, 2018, crash of a Tesla near Mountain View, CA. Unclear if automated control system was active at time of crash. Issues examined include: post-crash fire, steps to make vehicle safe for removal from scene.
— NTSB_Newsroom (@NTSB_Newsroom) March 27, 2018 . Meanwhile, Twitter, Inc. ( TWTR ) shares plummeted 12%, closing at $28.07, after short-seller Andrew Left's Citrion Research tweeted that the company would be "most vulnerable to privacy regulation."
Citron short $TWTR . Near-Term target $25 Of all social media, they are most vulnerable to privacy regulation Wait until Senate finds out what Citron has published. https://t.co/nAkRWb8Kcn
— Citron Research (@CitronResearch) March 27, 2018 Among the FAANG stocks, Facebook ( FB ) shares fell 4.9%, Apple ( AAPL ) dipped 2.6%, Amazon ( AMZN ) fell 3.8%, Netflix ( NFLX ) tumbled 6% and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) fell 4.6%. Microsoft ( MSFT ) shares fell 4.6%.
The Nasdaq fell 2.9% Tuesday, while the S&P 500 fell 1.7% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.4%.
